modules.description: Understand the service cycle, receiving, sorting, and recordkeeping that preserve linen identity and keep soiled and clean linen separate. This material and its simulations are original study practice. The official source reviewed names the linen-supply examination but has not published a blueprint, detailed syllabus, or exam format; do not treat the app's practice set as an official format.

sections.body:
Linen services are cyclical: hotels, hospitals, and other customers use supplied items; after use, the items are collected, processed, inspected, and returned. Products may include sheets, pillowcases, towels, patient garments, uniforms, and table linens. Workers follow the scope and standards of their facility.

Exam-information limit: the official source reviewed has not published a blueprint, detailed syllabus, or exam format for the linen-supply examination. The app's content and simulations are original study practice, not claims about the official exam format.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Record each lot under the customer's identity. Keep containers of unprocessed items separate from clean-product zones. Do not change labels or processing order based on a guess; if identity is missing, hold the lot and request confirmation so it remains traceable.

Practice case: A basket of sheets has no customer label, while another basket contains clean linen.
Recommended response: Separate the two baskets, do not guess who owns the sheets, and report the issue so their identity and routing can be confirmed.

sections.body: Check whether the product is clean, dry enough for the next stage, neat, free of tears or distortion, and the expected type. Visual checks or inspection tools support quality control, but criteria are set by the facility. Separate defective items with the correct status; do not hide a defect in a fold.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Inspect at designated checkpoints, including after a program change. If you find stains, holes, incorrect folds, odor, or a questionable size, separate the item and record its characteristics. Notify the relevant line so the process can be reviewed.

Practice case: Stains are found on several sheets from the same line.
Recommended response: Separate the sheets, record the defect and originating line, and report it so the preceding stage can be checked.

sections.body: Group linen that passes inspection by type, size, and customer. Bundle quantities and tying or packaging methods follow the order and facility standards; quantities are not always the same. Keep customer labels readable. A final count prevents shortages, excess, or order mix-ups.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use a table and packaging materials reserved for clean products. Count using the work unit, compare with the order sheet, and verify labels before moving items. If quantities do not match, hold the lot and ask for direction; do not make up the difference with another customer's items.

Practice case: One customer's order is short two towels, while extra towels belonging to another customer are available.
Recommended response: Do not substitute towels between customers. Record the discrepancy, hold order completion, and ask the person in charge to trace the quantities.

sections.body: Protect clean products from floors, dust, water, and soiled items. Use containers, carts, and shipping units according to facility rules and order identity. Organize routes to prevent goods from falling or becoming mixed. Storage and vehicle conditions must meet local standards.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Check that carts are undamaged, routes are clear, and labels are visible. Do not stack above safe limits or put products on the floor. If packaging is wet, torn, or falls into an unclean area, hold it and follow the reassessment procedure.

Practice case: A shipping container has liquid residue, and a bundle of clean linen is about to be loaded.
Recommended response: Delay loading and have the container cleaned and dried under procedure before placing clean products inside.

lessons.response: Record the time, visible indicator, safe actions taken, and pending-inspection status; hand this information to the next shift lead.
lessons.scenario: At shift change, one line is still stopped and the cause has not been identified.

sections.body: Production spans several stages and shifts. A useful handover gives the lot number, location, time, observed condition, actions taken, and people notified. Factual records prevent repeated checks and support traceability. Avoid vague terms without observable detail.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Complete records in the company system, mark held goods, and directly hand over risky issues. The receiving shift should repeat key information when anything is unclear. Do not mark a task complete until inspection or repair has actually taken place.

Practice case: At shift change, one line is still stopped and the cause has not been identified.
Recommended response: Record the time, visible indicator, safe actions taken, and pending-inspection status; hand this information to the next shift lead.
